jobs.title: AI Researcher
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The future of defense will be decided by those who field intelligent machines at scale. At Scout AI, we’re developing Fury, the first robotic foundation model for defense, to give U.S. forces overwhelming, adaptable, and autonomous power across every domain. Fury enables human operators to command fleets of robots through natural language, and empowers those machines to sense, decide, and act together as one. This mission will ask everything of us: urgency, precision, and relentless work.

The Role
We’re hiring an AI Researcher on the Fury Team to help push the frontiers of embodied intelligence for autonomous defense systems. You will lead research in core areas including reinforcement learning, vision-language-action modeling, sim-to-real transfer, dynamic AI memory, and multi-agent coordination. Your work will be foundational to the development, training, and deployment of Fury.

This role sits at the intersection of cutting-edge ML research, real-world robotics, and defense. You'll translate foundational research into scalable, robust models that operate in unstructured, contested environments, from concept to deployment. We’re a startup. You’ll be moving fast, context-switching daily, and helping define the culture and process as we go. This is a rare opportunity to come in early and architect the future of defense. 

Responsibilities

  • Conduct original research in embodied AI, including learning from warfighter demonstration, reinforcement learning, memory, reward, vision-language modeling, and world modeling

  • Build, test, and benchmark large-scale models for perception, decision-making, and control in simulated and physical environments

  • Investigate transfer learning and continual learning paradigms across diverse robotic domains

  • Collaborate with engineering, robotics, and field teams to integrate research into operational systems

  • Lead research strategy and roadmap across key areas of autonomy and machine learning

  • Support field tests and data collection campaigns to evaluate system performance in realistic environments

Qualifications

  • PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or a related field (or equivalent industry research experience)

  • Strong publication record in top-tier venues

  • Deep expertise in one or more of the following: reinforcement learning, imitation learning, vision-language models, sim-to-real, world modeling, or agentic AI

  • Hands-on experience building and evaluating models for embodied agents or autonomous systems

  • Proficiency in Python and frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX

  • Experience working with large-scale datasets and high-dimensional sensor inputs

  • Demonstrated ability to take ideas from research concept to deployed prototype

  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

  • Passion about defense of the United States and its allies

  • May be expected to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

Why Join Scout

  • Work on the world’s most important frontier, ensuring U.S. and allied dominance in the age of intelligent machines

  • Be a core part of a team building the first defense-specific robotic foundation model

  • Collaborate with some of the top engineers in autonomy, AI, and national security

  • See your work deployed on real systems

  • Help define the future of intelligent defense systems

  • Backed by Draper Associates, Booz Allen Ventures, and other top investors

Benefits

  • Competitive Cash Compensation

  • Meaningful equity

  • Premium medical, dental, and vision plans with $0 paycheck contribution

  • Competitive PTO and company holiday calendar

  • Catered lunch daily and fully stocked kitchen

  • EV charging

  • Relocation assistance (depending on role eligibility)

jobs.title: Mission Operator - Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The future of defense will be decided by those who field intelligent machines at scale. At Scout AI, we’re developing Fury, the first robotic foundation model for defense, to give U.S. forces overwhelming, adaptable, and autonomous power across every domain. Fury enables human operators to command fleets of robots through natural language, and empowers those machines to sense, decide, and act together as one. This mission will ask everything of us: urgency, precision, and relentless work.

The Role

We’re hiring Mission Operators to act as forward-deployed operators and field engineers for our unmanned ground vehicle programs. You’ll own system performance in real-world environments, executing field missions, supporting high-visibility customer demos, and ensuring platforms are mission-ready at all times. Operating at the intersection of engineering, operations, and customer engagement, you’ll run test events, operate autonomous systems, and troubleshoot issues across hardware and software in real time. You’ll work closely with engineers to validate performance, drive rapid iteration, and deliver actionable field feedback.

This is a hands-on, field-heavy role. You’ll deploy, operate, and recover systems in dynamic environments while maintaining high standards of safety, professionalism, and technical execution. You’ll also represent Scout in front of customers, clearly communicating system capabilities and performance under real-world conditions.

Responsibilities

  • Lead forward-deployed operation of autonomous and semi-autonomous ground systems in complex, real-world environments, supporting customer-facing demonstrations and field evaluations

  • Execute and adapt mission test plans in dynamic conditions, ensuring successful outcomes while maintaining strict safety and operational standards

  • Serve as the on-site technical authority during field operations, diagnosing and resolving mechanical, electrical, and software issues in real time

  • Interface directly with high-priority customers and stakeholders, briefing system capabilities, conducting live demonstrations, and representing product performance in the field

  • Coordinate end-to-end field logistics including system deployment, mobility, sustainment, and recovery across distributed test environments

  • Drive system readiness through hands-on maintenance, inspection, and rapid repair of vehicles, payloads, and supporting equipment

  • Capture and communicate actionable field insights to engineering and product teams, influencing system improvements and future development

  • Maintain operational awareness of system health, performance, and limitations to ensure mission success under austere conditions

  • Enforce and model disciplined safety practices for personnel, equipment, and autonomous system operations

Qualifications

  • Experience operating and sustaining vehicles, robotic systems, or complex field equipment in dynamic environments

  • Proficiency in off-road driving, trailering, and executing operations in austere or rugged conditions

  • Strong mechanical and electrical troubleshooting skills, with the ability to diagnose and resolve issues across hardware and software systems

  • High level of situational awareness with a disciplined approach to safety in field operations

  • Effective communicator under pressure, capable of coordinating with engineering teams and interfacing with customers in real time

  • Self-directed and adaptable, with the ability to operate independently in field-heavy, fast-paced environments

  • Willingness and enthusiasm to spend significant time outdoors supporting field missions and test operations

  • Mission-driven, with a strong interest in advancing autonomous systems for defense applications

  • Ability to travel 50–75% to support testing, deployments, and customer engagements

  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

  • Passion about defense of the United States and its allies

  • May be expected to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

At Scout, we’re developing Fury, the first robotic foundation model for defense, to give U.S. forces overwhelming, adaptable, and autonomous power across every domain. Fury enables human operators to command fleets of robots through natural language, and empowers those machines to sense, decide, and act together as one. This mission will ask everything of us: urgency, precision, and relentless work. We hope you’ll join us.

The Role
We're hiring for a Proposal Manager to drive world-class proposal execution across Scout AI's portfolio of government and commercial opportunities. You'll own the end-to-end proposal lifecycle, coordinating cross-functional teams to produce compliant, compelling responses to RFPs, RFIs, SBIRs, BAAs, and commercial bids. Think of this as the connective tissue between BD, Sales, Programs, Product, Engineering, Legal, and Finance: you'll keep teams aligned, on schedule, and focused on winning narratives. You'll report into Scout's growth organization and work daily with domain managers, engineering leadership, and the CEO to ensure proposals are technically sharp, strategically positioned, and submitted on time.

Responsibilities

  • Own proposal strategy and execution across all active pursuits: establish win themes, align technical approach, coordinate compliance review, and drive proposals to on-time submission

  • Serve as Proposal Lead on active opportunities: facilitate kickoffs, assign writing tasks, set detailed milestones, manage proposal schedules, and surface blockers early

  • Build and maintain a proposal asset library of reusable, high-quality templates including cover letters, SOWs, compliance matrices, cost volumes, organizational capability narratives, and past performance summaries

  • Translate technical concepts into evaluator-focused narratives: work with Engineering, Product, and Program teams to distill complex capabilities into clear, persuasive proposal language that resonates with government and commercial evaluators

  • Coordinate cross-functional reviews to stress-test win themes, validate compliance, confirm cost realism, and ensure all sections support a cohesive, differentiated story before submission

  • Manage proposal schedules and status tracking, including risk reporting, milestone tracking, and resource coordination across functions

  • Drive proposal operations and process improvement: establish scorecards, checklists, and workflows that enable consistent, scalable proposal execution as the company grows

  • Lead pricing and cost volume coordination between technical teams and Finance to ensure credible, competitive cost narratives that align with technical scope

  • Manage multiple concurrent proposals at varying stages of maturity, maintaining organized documentation, compliance artifacts, and version control

  • Ensure compliant submissions across government portals (SAM.gov, agency-specific systems) in partnership with BD and Sales

Qualifications

  • 8+ years in proposal management, program management, or government contracting within defense tech, space, dual-use, or equivalent professional experience

  • Proven track record leading proposals from kickoff through submission for SBIRs, RFPs, BAAs, or similar government solicitations

  • Strong technical communication skills: ability to distill engineering and product concepts into clear, evaluator-friendly narratives without over-simplifying

  • Foundational understanding of engineering, product development, and systems architecture to support credible technical scoping and writing

  • CRM and pipeline tool proficiency for deal tracking, reporting, and workflow management

  • Familiarity with government procurement processes, FAR/DFARS compliance, and common submission portals and timelines

  • Comfort with process building: ability to create and refine templates, scorecards, checklists, and workflows that scale and improve over time

  • APMP, PMP, or Shipley certification (or equivalent proposal management credential)

  • Experience in space, defense, Earth observation, or robotics sectors

  • Deep SBIR/STTR expertise, including Phase I → Phase II positioning strategy and program structure

  • Hands-on pricing experience including rate structures, LOE estimation, risk/reserve methodology, and budget narrative development

  • Experience with proposal automation tools or proposal writing platforms (Deltek, Responsive, Proposal software ecosystems)

  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

  • Passion about defense of the United States and its allies

  • May be expected to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

Why Join Scout

  • Work on the world’s most important frontier, ensuring U.S. and allied dominance in the age of intelligent machines

  • Be a core part of a team building the first defense-specific robotic foundation model

  • Collaborate with some of the top engineers in autonomy, AI, and national security

  • See your work deployed on real systems

  • Help define the future of intelligent defense systems

  • Backed by Draper Associates, Booz Allen Ventures, and other top investors

Benefits

  • Competitive cash compensation

  • Meaningful equity

  • Premium medical, dental, and vision plans with $0 paycheck contribution

  • Competitive PTO and company holiday calendar

  • Catered lunch daily and fully stocked kitchen

  • EV charging

  • Relocation assistance (depending on role eligibility)

The Role

As a Software Engineer on the Agent Harnessing team, you will build the core architecture that allows AI agents to interact with and control complex, real-world physical systems. This spans agent orchestration, tool integration, low-latency communication layers, and execution environments—designed as a platform that Scout AI engineers can extend and depend on.

  • Building simulation environments and video-game-like frameworks that allow agents to be tested and trained before physical deployment

  • Owning the connectors between AI models and real-world systems, the layer that translates model output into physical action

  • Fine-tune frontier AI models and build the data acquisition pipelines that feed the training infrastructure powering our agents

  • Work shoulder-to-shoulder with warfighters to turn capability requests into production-ready agentic systems

The future of defense will be decided by those who field intelligent machines at scale. Fury enables human operators to command fleets of robots through natural language, and empowers those machines to sense, decide, and act together as one. This mission will ask everything of us: urgency, precision, and relentless work.

The Role
We’re hiring a Drone Pilot to join our Mission Operations team at our test site in Paso Robles, CA. You’ll pilot and supervise uncrewed aerial systems during test flights, autonomy trials, and live mission rehearsals - operating both manually and in supervised-autonomy modes. This is a hands-on, field-based role for someone who is comfortable in the air, meticulous about safety, and energized by working at the frontier of defense robotics.

Responsibilities

  • Plan, set up, and execute drone flight operations in support of autonomy testing and mission rehearsals

  • Pilot uncrewed aerial systems manually and supervise autonomous flight, intervening safely when needed

  • Conduct pre-flight inspections, perform routine maintenance, and troubleshoot hardware and payload issues in the field

  • Capture, log, and organize flight data, telemetry, and observations to feed our model training and engineering teams

  • Enforce airspace, range, and safety protocols, and help maintain compliance with FAA and site regulations

  • Provide clear, structured feedback to engineers on system performance, failure modes, and edge cases

  • Support field deployments, including equipment transport, staging, and recovery

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience operating drones / uncrewed aerial systems (commercial, military, or equivalent)

  • FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate, or the ability to obtain one prior to start

  • Strong situational awareness, sound judgment under pressure, and an uncompromising commitment to safety

  • Comfort working outdoors in varied conditions at a test range, with the ability to lift and transport equipment

At Scout AI, we’re developing Fury, the first robotic foundation model for defense, to give U.S. forces overwhelming, adaptable, and autonomous power across every domain. Fury enables human operators to command fleets of robots through natural language, and empowers those machines to sense, decide, and act together as one. This mission will ask everything of us: urgency, precision, and relentless work.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior or Staff AI Engineer to join the Fury Orchestration Team with a deep passion for developing and deploying multimodal foundation models that power autonomous teams of robots. Your work will directly influence how our system reasons, plans, remembers and coordinates across multiple robots to accomplish long-horizon missions. Depending on your background and interests, you’ll contribute across the stack: model training and evaluation, reinforcement learning, evaluation and simulation, reasoning and memory architectures, multi-agent coordination, and edge inference optimization. Expect to rapidly prototype ideas against rigorous evaluations, test ideas on real robotic mission rollouts, and break new ground as we create the first robotic foundation model for defense.

We’re a startup. You’ll be moving fast, context-switching daily, and helping define the culture and process as we go. You’ll have substantial ownership, influence over technical direction, and the opportunity to help build the future of autonomous defense systems from the ground up.

Responsibilities

  • Design, train, and evaluate multimodal foundation models that enable multi-robot mission execution

  • Drive model development decisions including model architectures, data mixtures, curriculum design, and training recipes informed by rigorous experimentation

  • Curate and generate large-scale training datasets from both synthetic and real-world data engines

  • Develop memory, communication, planning, and tool-use capabilities for AI agents operating across teams of robots

  • Be obsessed with evaluation: design benchmarks, metrics, and testing methodologies that enable rapid iteration across the team

  • Build and improve simulation environments targeted for synthetic data generation, evaluation, and reinforcement learning

  • Translate foundational research into deployable, real-time perception and decision-making systems

  • Collaborate across engineering, robotics, and mission teams to integrate AI systems with onboard autonomy stacks

  • Conduct field trials and mission operations to validate system performance e under real-world constraints

Qualifications

  • Proficiency in Python, PyTorch, and modern machine learning infrastructure

  • Experience training, finetuning, and evaluating large-scale deep learning models using distributed compute infrastructure

  • Demonstrated experience improving model performance through data curation, training strategy, evaluation design, and rigorous experimentation

  • Solid grasp of modern model training techniques including SFT, DPO, RLVR

  • Support test campaigns and debugging efforts with engineering teams

  • Experience assembling and troubleshooting electrical systems and wiring harnesses

  • Familiarity with electronics tools (crimpers, multimeters, oscilloscopes, soldering equipment)

The future of defense will be decided by those who field intelligent machines at scale. Fury enables human operators to command fleets of robots through natural language, and empowers those machines to sense, decide, and act together as one. The Role

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer who treats the code itself as the product. You’ll join the core software team at Scout AI and work across the systems Fury runs on: the onboard C++ code and core libraries, the cloud infrastructure that trains and evaluates the model, and the simulation and evals framework that tells us whether any of it works.

A lot of this job is hardening. As our platform rapidly scales, our senior engineers actively drive architectural stewardship - continually refining abstractions, hardening core systems, and evolving our software foundation to support our accelerated growth. We want someone who can take that on: read a large codebase, understand it, spot the anti-patterns, and restructure it well.

The same person should be comfortable building the test and validation systems that let the rest of the team move faster. We aren’t hiring for one narrow specialty. Depending on where you’re strongest, you might spend most of your time onboard C++, in GPU job infrastructure and cloud services, or in simulation and evaluation tooling. What’s common across all of it is a background building frameworks and libraries that other systems depend on, rather than applications on top of someone else’s framework. We use AI coding tools and expect you to as well, but we think of them as a multiplier on skills you already have. You should be able to write, explain, and debug your own code without them.

We’re a startup. You’ll be moving fast, context-switching daily, and helping define the culture and process as we go. This is a rare opportunity to come in early and architect the future of defense.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain onboard C++ software and core system libraries

  • Build scalable, low-latency C++ and Python infrastructure for ML workloads

  • Design cloud systems for data storage and GPU job scheduling

  • Build simulation and evaluation pipelines, including synthetic agents, rendering tools, and scenario suites

  • Create evaluation criteria and internal tooling to analyze and compare software release builds

  • Refactor existing codebases to eliminate anti-patterns and improve system architecture

  • Construct data pipelines for sensor calibration and 3D reconstruction workflows

  • Implement automated test and validation frameworks across subsystem engineering teams

  • Proficient in C++ or Python (either is fine) for core systems, simulation, evaluation, and tooling work

  • Demonstrated experience navigating, auditing, and refactoring large codebases

  • Track record of building shared software frameworks or underlying libraries

  • Ability to write, debug, and explain complex code independently without relying on AI tools

  • Passion about defense of the United States and its allies

  • May be expected to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

  • Cloud and infrastructure experience (GPU job scheduling, service deployment)

Sunnyvale, CA

The future of defense will be decided by those who field intelligent machines at scale. The Role

We’re building autonomous vehicles and need a hands-on technician to keep our fleet healthy and help build new vehicles. This is one role with two main responsibilities. The larger segment is fleet ownership: you’re the person who knows the state of every vehicle, what it needs, and when it will be ready. The other portion is vehicle build and upfit, where you work from drawings and work instructions to help get new vehicles built.

You’ll sit on the Vehicle Integration team and be the link between Engineering and Mission Operations (MOPS), so you’ll need to be comfortable with both the wrenches and the tracking systems. You’ll be based at HQ, with regular travel to our testing facility. This is a chance to come in early and build the processes that keep a fleet of autonomous vehicles in the field.

Responsibilities

Fleet ownership (75%)

  • Own vehicle readiness: know which vehicles are up, down, or in service, and why

  • Track fleet health, issues, and repairs in Jira and Fleetio

  • Implement and run a preventive maintenance program, including schedules, service history, and follow-through

  • Coordinate with MOPS to schedule repairs and keep vehicles available for testing

  • Triage faults, decide what to fix in-house, and escalate to Engineering when it’s beyond base vehicle repair

  • Perform base vehicle repairs and maintenance as needed

  • Manage spares and parts inventory for the fleet

  • Transport vehicles between the testing facility and HQ when needed

  • Spot recurring failures and bring them back to Engineering and MOPS with data

Build and upfit (25%)

  • Help with vehicle upfits at HQ, including mounting, wiring, and installing hardware to work instructions and drawings

  • Follow checklists and record what was actually built, including serial numbers and any deviations from the drawing

  • Flag unclear instructions or mismatches to Engineering rather than guessing

  • Give feedback on work instructions so they get better over time

Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with vehicle, equipment, or electromechanical work (automotive, off-road/UTV, heavy equipment, robotics, or similar)

  • Comfortable using hand and power tools and following wiring diagrams and technical drawings

  • Experience owning maintenance or readiness for a fleet or set of equipment, or a clear ability to pick it up quickly

  • Organized, with a habit of documenting your work and keeping records current

  • Clear communicator who can work across Engineering and operations teams

  • Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record, and willingness to drive vehicles between sites

  • Passion about defense of the United States and its allies

Nice to have

  • Experience with Fleetio or another fleet maintenance system

  • Experience with Jira or similar issue tracking

  • Wire harness, connector termination, or CAN bus familiarity

  • Experience with autonomous, robotic, or prototype vehicles

The Role

We’re seeking a Mechanical Engineer Intern for Summer 2027 who is passionate about robotics, hardware, and building machines that hold up in the field. You'll work alongside our hardware and robotics engineers to design, build, and validate the mechanical systems that carry Fury onto real platforms, from vehicle testbeds to ruggedized compute enclosures and field-ready payload integrations. Your work will run on robots in demanding, adversarial environments. Expect to move fast, iterate on real systems, and see your designs tested outside the lab.

This 10-week internship is ideal for students looking to apply their engineering skills to high-stakes, real-world applications. You’ll gain exposure to the full hardware development loop, from napkin sketch to prototype to environmental testing, and work on systems that operate in real world conditions.

What You’ll Do

  • Support the design, build, and deployment of mechanical and electromechanical systems across Scout’s robotic platforms

  • Design and prototype rugged enclosures, brackets, mounts, and payload interfaces in 3D CAD

  • Help with component selection and integration for compute modules, communication devices, networking components, and sensors

  • Develop test fixtures and support hardware testing, including wiring, environmental sealing, and system validation

  • Integrate hardware with electrical and software systems in field-ready robotic platforms

  • Collaborate with mentors, mission operations, and the software and autonomy teams to turn field feedback into design improvements

  • Troubleshoot hardware in the shop and in the field

  • Author documentation for test plans, validation results, integration procedures, and hardware specs

  • Support field trials and mission operations to validate hardware performance under real-world constraints

Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field

  • Strong 3D CAD skills (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Onshape, or similar)

  • Solid grounding in engineering fundamentals such as statics, materials, thermal, and tolerancing

  • Hands-on experience building, fabricating, or testing hardware through coursework, a robotics or competition team, or personal projects

  • Comfortable navigating open-ended problems and proposing practical solutions

  • Strong communication and documentation skills

  • Bonus: Experience with ruggedized electronics, enclosure design, or environmental testing (thermal, shock and vibe, ingress protection)
